name: Nochi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: SIL PNG Branch. n.d. [printed 1 September 2004]. Organised Phonology Data: Nochi (Notsi) Language [NCF], Konos - New Ireland Province. 5 pp. Draft manuscript (posted without peer review), SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42417; its bibliography credits Erickson, Leland & Laurinda Erickson. 1990. 'Organized phonology data of the Nochi language.' Manuscript, SIL Ukarumpa.
catalog_quote: Stress is predictable and usually found on the final syllable, which is generally also the heaviest syllable in the word. If the first syllable is heavier, also the stress falls on the first syllable. Reduplicated two syllable words with each syllable identical in CV pattern and phoneme quality have equal stress on each syllable.
world_status: statement found in an open source

Nothing else on pp. 1-5 bears on stress (p. 3-4 give syllable patterns and allophonic conventions; pp. 4-5 a transcribed…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is predictable: it falls on the heaviest syllable, which is normally the final syllable; when the first syllable is heavier than the final, the first syllable is stressed. Identical-syllable disyllabic reduplications get equal stress on both syllables. Default reading: final stress with weight override (weight-sensitive; unbounded heavy-first vs. default-final).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (only 'equal stress' on both syllables of identical reduplications).
new_statements.exceptions: If the first syllable is heavier than the final one, stress falls on the first syllable; two-syllable reduplications whose syllables are identical in CV shape and segments carry equal stress on both syllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('found on the final syllable.. in the word'); based on SIL fieldworkers' phonology data (Erickson & Erickson 1990), no instrumental evidence; the OPD is a draft posted without peer review.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD names the language 'Nochi (Notsi) [NCF]', Konos area, villages Amba, Tandis, Lossu; Notsi = Nochi = Noatsi (Ross's PARADISEC label) = Glottolog nots1237. No dialect split is described; McCarthy 2000's texts come from Lossu and Libba villages.

sources.citation: King, Phil. 2007. An Acoustic Description of Central Vowels in Three Austronesian Languages of New Ireland. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2007-005. 21 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: No stress rule stated; only remarks that 'intonation and stress have more effect on the length of any individual vowel' (Tiang section, p.9) and that measurements from unstressed syllables under 45 ms were rejected. Notsi minimal pair on p.7 Table 4 is transcribed with stress marks [»tələ] 'here' vs [tə»la] 'there', consistent with stress on the heavier (a-) syllable.
